# Optional. The module works without any key here.
#
# By default the module sets ro.adb.secure=0.  On an unlocked bootloader
# (which Magisk requires) adbd then skips authorization entirely: just flash
# the zip, reboot, and `adb devices` shows `device`.  No key, no prompt.
#
# You only need to put a key here when:
#   * you set FORCE_INSECURE_ADB=0 in /data/adb/adb-enable/config, or
#   * your ROM ignores ro.adb.secure and insists on `unauthorized`.
#
# The key is generated by the PC the first time adb runs, no phone needed:
#   Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.android\adbkey.pub
#   Linux/macOS: ~/.android/adbkey.pub
#
# Recommended for a broken screen (TWRP shell is root):
#   adb shell "mkdir -p /data/adb/adb-enable/keys"
#   adb push adbkey.pub /data/adb/adb-enable/keys/pc.pub
# This module's own keys/ dir is also scanned, as is /data/local/tmp.
#
# /sdcard/adb-enable/keys/* is only read when KEYS_FROM_STORAGE=1.  It is off
# by default because any app with storage write access could add a key there
# and that key becomes permanently trusted.
#
# Accepted formats (one key per file, any visible file name):
#   QAAAA...                                     <- normal adbkey.pub
#   QAAAA... user@host
#   ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nza... user@host
#
# Files named README* or starting with a dot are ignored, as are files larger
# than 16 KiB and symlinks.
